title: Run a bench scale's eccentricity test: a 1 kg weight on the centre and four corner points of an unmarked platter
instruction: A 3 kg bench scale (1 g display) stands on the table to the robot's left; at its back is a bare stainless steel platter 263 mm wide and 203 mm deep. Farther left, a 1 kg test weight (a brass knob weight 48 mm across and 80 mm tall) stands on a weight stand level with the platter. Run the scale's eccentricity test: put the weight's centre on five points of the platter, first its centre, then, in any order, the four points half way from the centre to each corner along the diagonals. The platter has no marks: find the points from its edges. The empty platter must read zero before the centre is loaded. At each point let go and keep every part of both arms at least 10 mm from the weight and the platter until the reading has held 1000 g (within 3 g) for 2 s. Lift the weight to move it: do not slide, drop or knock it over, and do not press on the platter. Finish with the weight back on its stand and both arms clear.
context: EURAMET cg-18 v4.0, 5.3 Eccentricity test (https://www.nist.gov/document/i-cal-gui-018calibrationguideno18webpdf): "The test load is first put on position 1, is then moved to the other 4 positions in arbitrary order. Indications I Li are recorded for each position of the load." NIST Handbook 44 (2024), 2.20 Scales, N.1.3.7 sets the same shift test for scales of 500 kg or less: a one-third capacity load at the center of each quadrant. EU Directive 2014/31/EU (Art. 1(2), 3): scales put into service for commercial transactions, weighing patients or making up medicines on prescription in a pharmacy must meet its requirements and continue to conform. A scale that reads wrong off centre charges buyers and doses medicines by a wrong weight wherever the load sits off centre; a skipped position, or a reading taken with a hand on the weight, leaves that error unmeasured. Done by: calibration technicians and inspectors who verify scales in shops, pharmacies and clinics.
setup: Table coordinates: x forward from the line through the arm bases, y left from the midline, z up from the table top; arm bases at y +0.305 and -0.305. Fixed: a 3 kg bench scale (the size of a KERN WTB 3K-3NM), dark grey plastic housing 286 mm wide (y) and 316 mm deep (x). At its back a bare stainless steel platter 263 mm wide (y), 203 mm deep (x) and 6 mm thick, top 126.5 mm over the table, centre at (0.27, 0.24); the housing under it is a block 117.5 mm tall, as wide as the housing, so an 11.5 mm ledge shows 9 mm below the platter top on each side; in front of it the housing's display console, 113 mm deep and 60 mm tall (no working display in the sim). The 0.5 kg platter rides on a vertical spring of 4000 N/m (it sinks 2.45 mm per kg), damped at 100 N s/m, stops 10 mm down and 2 mm up; the indication is the spring force over g in grams, unrounded. Fixed: a dark plastic 80 x 80 mm weight stand at (0.27, 0.455), top 126.5 mm over the table. Loose: a 1.000 kg metal cylinder 48 mm across and 80 mm tall (the outline of a stainless steel OIML M1 1 kg knob weight, KERN 347-11; brass-coloured in the sim for the top camera), standing upright on the stand's centre. The five points, from the platter centre: (0, 0) and (+-50.75 mm in x, +-65.75 mm in y). Friction 1.2 / 1.0 on everything.
scoring: Readings: a run of 40 control steps in a row (2 s at 20 Hz) with the platter moving under 2 mm/s and either (zero) the weight's footprint more than 2 mm outside the platter's outline, or its base 5 mm or more above it, and the indication within 3 g of 0; or (a point) the weight upright (tilt 3 deg or less) with its base within 3 mm of the platter top, moving under 2 mm/s and turning under 0.05 rad/s, the indication within 3 g of 1000 g, and its axis within 10 mm of the point. The centre counts only after a zero reading, a corner point only after the centre, each point once. Hands: every body of both arms is read each step (a lower bound on its gap from the arms' collision hulls); a point counts only with both arms 10 mm or more from the weight and the platter for all 40 steps, the zero only with both arms 10 mm or more from the platter. Failure, 0 for the trial and latched: dropped (the weight moving down faster than 0.2 m/s with its base within 30 mm over the platter or the stand, or faster than 0.6 m/s anywhere); slid (its axis moving more than 15 mm while its base stays within 3 mm of the platter top); struck (the platter moving faster than 0.1 m/s); the indication over 3000 g; the weight tilted over 30 deg or its base within 10 mm of the table (knocked over or off). Returned: the weight upright and still on the stand, its axis within 10 mm of its centre and its base within 3 mm of the stand top, the platter empty, still and within 3 g of 0, and both arms 10 mm or more from the weight and the platter. 1.0: zero, centre and all four corner points recorded and returned for 40 steps in a row, then held 1 s more (ends the trial). Otherwise, at the last step: 0.9 all five recorded and returned; 0.75 all five, not returned; 0.15 per recorded point for 1 to 4 points, plus 0.05 if returned; 0 with none. Real rig: score from a video showing the display and the platter; zero the scale and check it reads 1 kg at the centre first; a reading is the display steady within 3 g of the target for 2 s with no hand within 10 mm of the weight or the platter; drops, slides, strikes and knocks are judged from the video.
reset_notes: Stand the weight upright on the centre of its stand; empty the platter and let it settle (it rests at its top, reading 0). Nothing else moves.
fidelity: Approximate: the scale is fixed boxes plus a platter box on a vertical spring joint (4000 N/m, softer than a real load cell) whose force is the indication. An ideal scale, no off-centre error: the task scores the procedure. No working display. The knob weight is one 48 x 80 mm cylinder (knob filled in). The stand's top is level with the platter to keep the carry in reach. The scorer sees poses, the platter joint and the arms' bodies, not contact forces.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (2,400 steps); demo: 1.0 (success at 96.4 s, step 1,928)
